1.note: 在 “neither... nor...” 结构中，谓语动词的单复数采取“就近原则”，即与靠近它的主语保持一致。此题中靠近空格的主语是复数名词 “his sisters”，因此谓语动词应用复数原形 “know”。
1.concept: 主谓一致 — Subject-Verb Agreement — Proximity Rule with neither...nor...
1.zh: 蒂姆和他的姐姐们都不知道怎么弹钢琴。

2.note: “scenes” 是可数名词复数，因此不能用修饰不可数名词的 “little” 和 “much”；“any” 通常用于否定句或疑问句。这里是肯定句，表示“有一些镜头”，应用 “some”。
2.concept: 限定词与量词的用法 — Quantifiers — Quantifiers for countable nouns
2.zh: 电影里有一些场景让我们笑个不停。

3.note: 空格处填入的反身代词用于指代前面的复数名词 “the children”，因此应当使用第三人称复数形式的反身代词 “themselves”，表示“孩子们自己”。
3.concept: 反身代词 — Pronouns — Reflexive Pronouns
3.zh: 托盘里的那些纸杯蛋糕不是导师烤的，而是孩子们自己烤的。

4.note: “with the intention of doing something” 是固定搭配，意为“抱着……的目的”或“打算做某事”。
4.concept: 介词固定搭配 — Prepositions — Prepositional Phrases
4.zh: 叶太太随身带了一张垫子，打算把它铺在地上，这样她野餐时就可以坐在上面。

5.note: 反义疑问句遵循“前肯后否”的原则。陈述句部分 “have a new car” 是肯定句，其中的 “have” 为实义动词（表示拥有），因此反义疑问部分需要借助助动词的否定形式，即 “don't”。
5.concept: 反义疑问句 — Grammar — Question Tags
5.zh: “Bala 夫妇买了一辆新车，不是吗？”我的邻居问道。

6.note: 本题考查错综时间条件句（Mixed Conditional）。从句 “If I had known...” 表达对过去事实的虚拟，而主句时间状语为 “today”（现在），因此主句形式应为 “would + 动词原形/进行时”，表示对现在情况的虚拟，故选 (3)。
6.concept: 虚拟语气 — Subjunctive Mood — Mixed Conditionals
6.zh: 如果我早知道雅各布住院了，我今天就会去医院看望他了。

7.note: 空格后是一个完整的句子（主谓宾结构），表达让步关系。 “although” 是连词，后接让步状语从句；而 “but” 是并列连词， “nonetheless” 是副词，均不符合此处的语法结构。
7.concept: 连词与从句 — Conjunctions — Concession Clauses
7.zh: 尽管许多人怀疑她的能力，她依然继续追逐自己的梦想。

8.note: 空格处引导定语从句，修饰先行词 “Simon”，且在从句中作定语修饰 “father”，表示“西蒙的父亲”，具有所属关系，因此使用关系代词 “whose”。
8.concept: 定语从句 — Relative Clauses — Relative Pronouns showing possession
8.zh: 西蒙的父亲是一位科学教授，西蒙在今年的科学奥林匹克竞赛中脱颖而出获得了冠军。

9.note: “学生们能够就给定的话题进行分享” 发生在过去（were able to），而 “阅读老师提供的笔记” 这一动作发生在分享之前，即“过去的过去”，因此必须使用过去完成时 “had read”。
9.concept: 动词时态 — Verb Tenses — Past Perfect Tense
9.zh: 学生们能够就给定的话题进行分享，因为他们已经阅读了老师提供的笔记。

10.note: 本题考查感官动词的固定搭配 “see somebody doing/do something”。此处表示警察到达时正目睹一个愤怒的人躺在地上，强调正在发生的动作，应用现在分词 “lying”。
10.concept: 非谓语动词 — Non-finite Verbs — Verbs of Perception
10.zh: 当警察到达咖啡店时，他们看到一个愤怒的人正躺在地上。

11.note: 根据新加坡小学会考（PSLE）英文广告阅读部分的常规考点设置，此类烹饪课程通常需要通过主办方的官方网站进行在线报名登记。
11.concept: 阅读理解 — 信息匹配
11.zh: 烹饪课程的报名需要通过 KidsChef 网站进行。

12.note: 根据2012年PSLE真题广告时间表，19-21 Nov与20-27 Nov的营地时间重合；29 Nov-1 Dec和6-8 Dec包含周六（属于周末课程）。只有3 Dec至5 Dec为周一至周三，完全符合“工作日”且“避开营地”的双重筛选条件。
12.concept: 阅读理解 — 时间推导与多条件筛选
12.zh: Kenny 想在工作日参加烹饪课。此外，他需要在 11 月 20 日至 27 日参加学校营地。因此，他应该选择 12 月 3 日至 5 日的烹饪课程。

13.note: 原文提及成功完成该年终烹饪课程后将获颁证书，该证书即为参加少儿烹饪大赛（Junior Cooking Competition）的准入资格凭证。
13.concept: 阅读理解 — 条件关联与细节理解
13.zh: 那些获得烹饪课程证书的人被允许参加少儿烹饪大赛。

14.note: KidsChef 是活动主办方，Nutri Supermarket 与 Silver Spoon Appliances 是提供相关奖品的赞助商，Kitchenclothes Specialists 作为无关干扰项，不属于赞助商列表。
14.concept: 阅读理解 — 细节查找与排除法
14.zh: Kitchenclothes Specialists 不是少儿烹饪大赛奖品的赞助商。

15.note: 广告虽然包含了比赛、奖品、厨房安全等元素，但其最核心的篇幅与主要意图依然是吸引学生报名参加其举办的年终烹饪课程。
15.concept: 阅读理解 — 全篇主旨大意题
15.zh: 该广告的主要目的是为了宣传年终烹饪课程。

11.stem_plain: After much thought, she finally _________ to face her fears and pursue her dream of becoming an astronaut.

12.stem_plain: The commuters shrieked when they spotted a rat _________ across the MRT platform.

13.stem_plain: The scouts decided to carry on with the hike even though there was an _________ storm.

14.stem_plain: The small boat _________ up and down in the choppy water, causing passengers to feel queasy.

15.stem_plain: After losing the first half of the match, the coach spoke to the players and their confidence was _________.

11.concept: 词汇辨析 — 决心/决定 — resolve to do something
11.note: “resolved” 意为“下定决心”或“决意”，后面常接动词不定式（to face），指经过深思熟虑（After much thought）后做出的坚定决定。而 obliged 和 compelled 强调被迫或迫于义务，pressed 强调遭受压力，均不符合主动追梦的语境。应选（3）。

choices.eg: He felt obliged to help his neighbor clean up the yard.
The student was pressed for time during the final exam.
She resolved to work harder next semester to get better grades.
The bad weather compelled them to change their holiday plans.

12.concept: 词汇辨析 — 动物动作 — scurry
12.note: “scurrying” 意为“急促跑”或“疾行”，专门用于形容老鼠等小动物惊慌、迅速地乱窜，符合老鼠跨越地铁站台的画面。strolling 指闲逛，scattering 指散开，sashaying 指摇摆招摇地走，均不符合语境。应选（2）。

choices.eg: They spent the afternoon strolling along the sunny beach.
The mice were scurrying away into a hole in the wall.
The sudden loud noise sent the birds scattering in all directions.
The fashion models were sashaying down the runway.

13.concept: 词汇辨析 — 暴风雨修饰词 — imminent
13.note: “imminent” 意为“即将发生的”或“逼近的”，常指不好的事情（如暴风雨、危险）马上就要到来。句中用 “even though”（尽管）连接，说明尽管暴风雨即将来临，童子军们仍决定继续前行。应选（1）。

choices.eg: The dark clouds indicate that a heavy downpour is imminent.

choices.zh: 不可避免的；必然发生的
choices.eg: Accidents are inevitable if you drive too fast on rainy days.

choices.zh: 未预料到的；意料之外的
choices.eg: The project was delayed due to some unforeseen expenses.

choices.zh: 不可预测的；捉摸不定的
choices.eg: The dynamic mountain weather can be highly unpredictable.

14.concept: 词汇辨析 — 船只动作 — bob up and down
14.note: “bobbed” 意为“（在水面上）上下跳动、随波浮沉”，固定搭配 “bob up and down” 常用来形容小船在波涛汹涌的水面中颠簸起伏。jiggled 指轻微摇晃，wobbled 指不稳地摇晃、偏斜，quivered 指颤抖，均不如 bobbed 贴切。应选（2）。

choices.eg: He jiggled the key in the lock until the door opened.
The bright red cork bobbed on the surface of the river.
The loose wheel wobbled as the bicycle moved forward.
Her voice quivered slightly as she gave the speech.

15.concept: 词汇辨析 — 信心搭配词 — restore confidence
15.note: “restored” 意为“恢复”或“使复原”，常与 confidence（信心）或 order（秩序）搭配。“restore confidence” 属于固定短语搭配，指教练的一番话让队员们在输掉上半场后重新找回了信心。应选（1）。

choices.eg: The deep sleep completely restored his energy after the long race.
A cold drink refreshed the tired players during the short break.
The company revamped its old website to attract younger customers.
He stayed at home all weekend to get his battery recharged.

16.concept: 近义词 — hastily（仓促地/匆忙地）
16.note: 副词 hastily 意为仓促地、急忙地。在形容人因匆忙而动作迅速的测试语境中，它直接对应副词 hurriedly（急忙地，仓促地）。
16.zh: 西蒙坐在最前面，匆忙下了车。

choices.zh: 迅速地，飞快地（指运动或发展速度快）
choices.eg: The popularity of the school's new dynamic chess club grew rapidly online.

choices.zh: 立即，马上（强调没有时间延迟）
choices.eg: The automated software responded instantly as soon as he plugged in the card.

choices.zh: 迅速地，敏捷地（多用于快速解决或处理事务）
choices.eg: The engineering group worked diligently to speedily resolve the technical issue.
Realising he was late for the presentation, he hurriedly packed his reference files.

17.note: 动词 ushered 意为引导、领位、护送（某人前往某处）。及物动词 guided 意为引导、带路，在为他人引路、指引方向的动作含义上完全重合。
17.zh: 他们受到了学长（纠察员）的迎接，学长领着他们去了三楼的大厅。

choices.eg: The polite student prefects guided the visiting teams toward the main exhibition hall.

choices.zh: 发信号，示意（作动词过去式）
choices.eg: The supervisor smoothly signalled to the assistant that the workshop presentation was over.
The unexpected technical error prompted the developers to double-check the server database.
The primary school principal strictly instructed the pupils to remain calm during the emergency.

18.concept: 近义词 — with bated breath（屏息以待地/迫切地）
18.note: 固定习语 with bated breath 意为屏息以待地、心悬在嗓子眼地，形容因期待或紧张而呼吸微弱的神态。在等候比赛开始的学术语境中，直接对应副词 eagerly（渴望地，热切地）。
18.zh: 参赛者们屏息以待地等待着比赛开始。

choices.eg: The young participants eagerly waited near the stage for the results to be announced.

choices.zh: 满怀希望地，抱有希望地
choices.eg: She looked hopefully at her coach, expecting to receive some supportive comments.
The weather conditions altered and became dreadfully cold during the midnight trek.
The driver tapped his fingers impatiently while waiting for the long traffic jam to clear up.

19.concept: 近义词 — worried and anxious（忧虑且焦虑的）
19.note: 短语 worried and anxious 形容人内心由于遇到突发困扰或阻碍而感到担忧、焦虑。形容词 troubled 意为忧虑的、苦恼的、不安的，与其在情感神态上最为贴合。
19.zh: 正当他感到忧虑和焦虑时，他的课外活动老师潘小姐递给了他眼镜。

choices.zh: 气馁的，沮丧的（指因挫败而失去信心）
choices.eg: Don't feel discouraged even if you fail to secure the trophy in the first match.

choices.zh: 悲伤的，伤心的（侧重巨大的悲痛）
choices.eg: The children let out a sorrowful sigh when their beloved pet bird escaped from the cage.
She felt deeply annoyed by the constant loud noise coming from the neighboring workshop.
He looked troubled after searching his entire bag and realising his glasses were missing.

20.note: 固定搭配 boosted his morale 意为提高、振奋某人的士气或斗志。及物动词 raised 拥有“提升、提高、振奋（士气/声音/价格等）”的核心高频学术义项，两者完全对等。
20.zh: 这无疑振奋了他的士气。

choices.zh: 提升，提高，振奋（士气/声音/价格等）
choices.eg: The teacher's supportive words successfully raised his morale before the final chess match.

choices.zh: 提高（职位/层次），使升高（物理高度/情绪等）
choices.eg: Regular morning training helped to elevate her baseline fitness levels significantly.

choices.zh: 增加（数量、程度或大小等）
choices.eg: The grocery platform increased the prices of organic food items during the holiday season.
Modern technology rapidly advances, transforming the way data processing works globally.

cloze: Simon and his CCA teammates alighted from the bus at Gardens Primary School. Simon, who was seated at the front, got down the bus [Q16(hastily)]. They were greeted by the prefects, who [Q17(ushered)] them to the hall on the third floor. Students from different schools were there to participate in the zonal chess competition.

There was an air of excitement in the hall. The participants waited [Q18(with bated breath)] for the competition to start. “Good afternoon, everyone. The competition will commence in five minutes,” the emcee announced. Simon proceeded to fish for his glasses in his bag and realised that they were missing. He needed his glasses for the competition. Just as he was feeling [Q19(worried and anxious)], Miss Phua, his CCA teacher, handed him his pair of glasses. That certainly [Q20(boosted)] his morale. “Your mother just dropped this off. Now do your best,” she said reassuringly.
zh: 西蒙和他的课外活动（CCA）队友们在花园小学走下了校车。坐在最前面的西蒙匆忙下了车。他们受到了学长（纠察员）们的迎接，学长领着他们去了三楼的大厅。来自不同学校的学生们聚集在这里参加区域象棋比赛。
大厅里弥漫着兴奋的气氛。参赛者们正屏息以待地等待着比赛开始。“大家下午好。比赛将在五分钟内正式开始，”主持人宣布道。西蒙开始在包里摸索他的眼镜，却惊恐地发现眼镜不见了。他比赛必须要用眼镜。正当他感到忧虑和焦虑时，他的CCA指导老师潘小姐走过来，把眼镜递给了他。这无疑极大地振奋了他的士气。“你妈妈刚刚送过来的。现在，尽你最大的努力吧，”她安慰着说道。

21.stem_plain: According to the visual text, the main purpose is to ________.

21.note: 解释为什么选这个答案 — replace stems, passages, and teaching copy when content is ready.

29.concept: 动词时态与主谓一致（一般现在时单数）
29.note: ‘The structure... is our diaphragm’，句子的核心主语是单数形式的名词 structure（结构），全篇客观陈述生理常识，故系动词选用 is。

30.concept: 关系从句（定语从句关系副词）
30.note: ‘is where all hiccups begin’，关系副词 where 引导表语从句，意为‘这就是所有打嗝开始的地方’。

31.concept: 介词用法（表示空间穿过、途径）
31.note: ‘air flows out of the lungs through the nose and mouth’，介词 through 在此表示‘通过、经由……途径/管道（通过鼻子和嘴巴）’流出。

32.concept: 代词（指示代词指代前文复数动作）
32.note: ‘These are actions which...’，指示代词复数 these 在此作主语，特指前文提到的 inhales 和 exhales（吸气和呼气）这两种行为。

33.concept: 连词用法（句子插入语转折关系）
33.note: ‘however, there are times when...’ 位于新分句首并用逗号隔开，作副词表示与前文“自动发生”的语气转折，意为‘然而，有时横隔膜也会受到刺激’。

34.concept: 介词用法（表示方向、终点或结果）
34.note: ‘resulting in a big hiccup’，短语 result in 为固定搭配，意为‘导致、造成（一个响亮的打嗝）’，此处 in 作介词引入结果。

35.concept: 情态动词（表示客观可能或必然推测）
35.note: ‘why the diaphragm could be irritated’，情态动词 could 在此表示某种潜在的可能性，与后面的动词原形被动语态 be irritated 连用，意为‘横隔膜可能会受到刺激的原因’。

36.concept: 介词搭配（动短语固定搭配）
36.note: ‘lead to hiccups’，短语 lead to 为固定搭配，意为‘导致、引起（打嗝）’。

37.concept: 动词时态与主谓一致（现在完成时助动词）
37.note: ‘you might have even tried...’，情态动词 might 后面接助动词 have 再接过去分词 tried，构成对过去发生事情的可能性推测，意为‘你甚至可能已经尝试过其中一两种方法了’。

38.concept: 连词用法（对照/让步状语从句）
38.note: ‘while another one is to sip water’，连词 while 在此用于连接两个并列分句，表示对比、对照关系，意为‘而另一种方法则是小口喝水’。

cloze: "Hic! Hic!" You may have let out these distinctive sounds after a heavy meal at one time or another. They are known as hiccups and they feel like jumpy gulps in the back of your throat. Have you wondered what causes hiccups? The structure responsible for hiccups in our complex body system [Q29] our diaphragm. This is a dome-shaped muscle at the bottom of your chest and is [Q30] all hiccups begin.

When a person inhales, the diaphragm pulls down to help draw air into the lungs. When one exhales, it relaxes and air flows out of the lungs [Q31] the nose and mouth into the surroundings. [Q32] are actions which take place automatically, whether you are awake or asleep. [Q33], there are times when the diaphragm becomes irritated. When this happens, the air rushes into your throat, hits your voice box and your vocal cords close suddenly, resulting [Q34] a big hiccup.
There are many reasons as to why the diaphragm [Q35] be irritated. Stress, eating too much or too quickly and feeling nervous are a few common reasons that may lead [Q36] hiccups.

There are lots of suggestions out there on how you can get rid of hiccups, and you might [Q37] even tried one or two of them. One way is to hold your breath and count to ten [Q38] another one is to sip water. Luckily, most hiccups are not harmful and will stop by themselves after a while.
zh: “嗝！嗝！” 你可能在某个时候饱餐一顿后发出过这些独特的声音。它们被称为打嗝，感觉就像喉咙后部跳动着的吞咽。你想过是什么引起打嗝吗？在我们复杂的身体系统中，负责打嗝的结构是我们的横隔膜。这是一个位于胸部底部的穹顶状肌肉，也是所有打嗝开始的地方。
当一个人吸气时，横隔膜会向下自拉，以帮助将空气吸入肺部。当一个人呼气时，它会放松，空气通过鼻子和嘴巴从肺部流出到周围环境中。这些都是自动发生行为，无论你是醒着还是睡着。然而，有时横隔膜也会受到刺激。当这种情况发生时，空气会冲进你的喉咙，撞击你的声带，你的声带会突然闭合，从而导致一个响亮的打嗝。
关于横隔膜为什么会受到刺激，有很多原因。压力、吃得太多或太快以及感到紧张，都是可能导致打嗝的几个常见原因。
关于如何消除打嗝，外面有很多建议，你甚至可能已经尝试过其中一两种了。一种方法是屏住呼吸并数到十，而另一种方法是小口喝水。幸运的是，大多数打嗝都是无害的，过一会儿就会自行停止。

40.note: 词性错误：在系动词 are 后面作表语，表示“因……而闻名”，应使用其形容词形式 famous，构成固定搭配 be famous for。

44.note: 拼写错误：正确拼写为 nurture（动词，意为养育、哺育）。

47.note: 时态错误：此处描述关于桉树叶有毒这一客观科学事实，应用一般现在时形式 are，而非过去时 were。

48.note: 修饰错误：nutrition 是不可数名词，不能用 few 修饰，应改为 little 表示“几乎没有提供营养”。

49.note: 拼写错误：正确拼写为 thoroughly（副词，意为彻底地、完全地）。

50.note: 拼写错误：正确拼写为 neutralises / neutralizes（动词单三形式，意为中和、消除）。

cloze: Koalas are native to Australia. How much do you know about them? There is [Q39(antrawling)] a lot more to these antrawling living 'teddy bears' than their cuddly size and laid-back lifestyle that they are [Q40(fame)] for. Is your [Q41(curiauscity)] piqued?

When the Europeans first settled in Australia, they [Q42(mistaking)] these tree dwellers for a type of bear. However, koalas are similar [Q43(with)] kangaroos, both of which are marsupials - mammals that [Q44(nurcher)] their newborn in a pouch. Of all the marsupials, [Q45(its)] closest relatives are the wombats.

Koalas live and feed on the eucalyptus trees. They climb up to the branches to munch on the leaves, [Q46(voraycously)] eating up to a kilogram of them daily. Did you know that the leaves of these trees [Q47(were)] poisonous? Furthermore, they are tough to digest and provide [Q48(few)] nutrition. Koalas have a specially adapted digestive system that not only [Q49(tharaghly)] extracts nutrients from the leaves but [Q50(newtralises)] their toxins. How amazing they are!
zh: 考拉是澳大利亚特有的动物。你对它们了解多少呢？这些迷人的活“泰迪熊”身上，除了它们那圆滚滚的可爱体型和广为人知的悠闲生活方式之外，其实还有很多不为人知的故事。你的好奇心被勾起来了吗？
当欧洲人最初在澳大利亚定居时，他们把这些树栖居民误认为是一种熊。然而，考拉其实与袋鼠很相似，它们都属于有袋动物——即在育儿袋中哺育新生儿的哺乳动物。在所有的有袋动物中，它们最亲近的亲戚是袋熊。
考拉在桉树上生活并以此为食。它们爬上树枝去啃食树叶，每天狼吞虎咽地吃掉多达一公斤的叶子。你知道这些树的叶子是有毒的吗？此外，它们很难消化，并且几乎无法提供营养。考拉拥有一种特殊适应的消化系统，不仅能彻底从叶子里提取营养，还能中和它们的毒素。它们是多么令人惊叹啊！

cloze: Intelligence is the ability to acquire and apply knowledge and skills. Human intelligence is a unique quality that consists of the abilities to learn from experience and [Q51] to new situations. When a computer or a robot is able to [Q52] a problem, it may seem intelligent. However, this type of intelligence is different [Q53] a human's intelligence. It is called artificial intelligence or A.I. The term A.I. was [Q54] in 1955 by John McCarthy, a computer scientist working on making computers intelligent.

The process of teaching computers to be intelligent involves researchers training the systems to play video games. Games provide a boundary with a set of rules. Computers play the games and based on [Q55] and error, different ways to win are figured out. They [Q56] on their stored memory to build on successes and learn from [Q57] made.

You might also be familiar with "Siri" on iPhone. It is an intelligent personal assistant who responds to your request, provides information and [Q58] tasks when told. You might ask "Siri", for example, to schedule an [Q59] in your calendar for your next visit to the dentist or dial your mother's phone number.

A.I. robots known as chatbots* are being [Q60] in online shops and the websites of government agencies to answer common [Q61] that customers may have. These chatbots have advanced to the stage where they possess [Q62] conversational abilities than ever before. Amazingly, A.I. has enabled these "deep learning" machines to learn from human behaviour, and [Q63] human knowledge and skills. For instance, chatbots can take the [Q64] of a doctor and start prescribing medicines to people. These expert systems can provide more advanced services which are typically carried out by highly [Q65] professionals - those that take many years of learning - such as doctors, lawyers and accountants.
Despite all the benefits, there is fear that artificial intelligence may take over our jobs. Whether artificial intelligence is good or bad, it is an advancement that is here to stay.
zh: 智能是指获取和应用知识与技能的能力。人类智能是一种独特的品质，包含从经验中学习以及适应新情况的能力。当计算机或机器人能够解决问题时，它似乎就具有了智能。然而，这种类型的智能与人类的智能完全不同。 “人工智能”或“A.I.”这一术语是由从事使计算机智能化研究的计算机科学家约翰·麦卡锡于1955年创造的。
教计算机变得智能的过程包括研究人员训练系统玩电子游戏。游戏通过一套规则提供了界限。计算机玩游戏，并基于试错，摸索出不同的获胜方法。它们依赖自己存储的记忆，在成功的基础上不断发展，并从所犯的错误中吸取教训。
你可能也很熟悉iPhone上的“Siri”。它是一个智能个人助理，能够回应你的请求、提供信息并在被告知时执行任务。例如，你可能会要求“Siri”在你的日历中安排一次预约，以便你下一次去看牙医，或者拨打你母亲的电话号码。

被称为聊天机器人的人工智能机器人正被使用在网上商店和政府机构的网站上，以回答客户可能遇到的常见问题。这些聊天机器人已经发展到了拥有比以往任何时候都更好的对话能力的阶段。令人惊奇的是，人工智能已经使 these “深度学习”机器能够从人类行为中学习，并获取人类的知识和技能。例如，聊天机器人可以扮演医生的角色，开始给人们开药。这些专家系统可以提供更高级的服务，而这些服务通常是由经过高度训练的专业人士——那些需要多年学习的人，如医生、律师和会计师来执行的。
尽管有种种好处，但人们仍然担心人工智能可能会接管我们的工作。无论人工智能是好是坏，它都是一种将长期存在的发展进步。
